tasks.agent_task: Implement the AWS Clean Rooms Service mock for this moto checkout. Follow the cleanrooms botocore service model as the API contract: collaborations, memberships, and configured tables with full CRUD, pagination, and resource tagging, with unknown resources raising the modeled not-found error. Create moto/cleanrooms/ with the same layout as existing services and register the backend in moto/backends.py and moto/backend_index.py. Preserve existing service conventions and backward compatibility.
notes: FUTURE 20afea38 is a squash-merged single-parent commit directly on C0 (verified with git rev-parse).
Offline gate A: the ground-truth patch applied to C0 passes 23/23 upstream tests. Blind gate B: an agent with no access to the future implementation or tests passed all 22 unit tests.
The API contract is discoverable in the environment via the botocore cleanrooms service model, so the task works under held-out tests.
C0 contains 173 service directories and cleanrooms is absent; six comparable services form the Signal extraction input.
tests/test_cleanrooms/test_server.py requires flask and flask-cors and is excluded; 22 of 23 upstream tests remain.
tests/test_dsql has 2 pre-existing failures in the reference environment; the regression selection avoids it.

tasks.agent_task: Implement DigitalOcean Spaces as an S3-compatible Libcloud storage provider. Add provider registration, supported-region validation and endpoint selection, independent AWS Signature V2/V4 connection selection, and reuse the existing S3 container and object behavior. Preserve existing storage driver conventions and backward compatibility.
tasks.regression_test_command: python3 -m pytest -q libcloud/test/storage/test_s3.py libcloud/test/storage/test_rgw.py libcloud/test/storage/test_google_storage.py libcloud/test/storage/test_azure_blobs.py libcloud/test/storage/test_cloudfiles.py
notes: The future commit is a single-parent commit directly after c0.
Its ten test methods use local objects and do not require a DigitalOcean account.

tasks.agent_task: Implement Google Cloud Storage as a Celery result backend. Register the gs backend URL, add gcs_* configuration, support byte keys and get/set/delete/mget operations, validate TTL and bucket lifecycle requirements, and provide a thread-safe cached client that is recreated after fork. Add optional dependency metadata and preserve existing Celery backend conventions.
notes: The merge commit has one parent and is directly after c0.
The future tests mock GCS clients and blobs; they do not require cloud credentials or a live service.
